brand.headline: Deep dish. No apologies.
brand.intro: Chicago deep dish with an Ozark accent: cornmeal-butter crust, okra in the giardiniera, and sorghum where you least expect it. Pull up a chair. Bring a fork.
brand.note: Windy Holler is a fictional parody pizzeria. Every name, address, phone number, dish, price, and story on this site is invented. Not affiliated with any real restaurant or with the University of Arkansas.

image.alt: Cast-iron pan of Chicago-style deep-dish pizza with a lifted slice and melted mozzarella cheese pull.

story: A Chicago pizza moved to the Ozarks and started borrowing from the neighbors: sorghum in the wing glaze, okra in the giardiniera, chocolate gravy on the brownie. Nobody in either state asked for this. Both states keep coming back.
ticker: Okra in the giardiniera, on purpose
Deep dish: a pizza with a basement

news.title: Deep dish completes first Pig Trail crossing without spilling
news.text: A 12-inch Chicago-style pie has crossed the Pig Trail from the river valley to Fayetteville with every layer intact. Witnesses credit the crust walls, which were built to Chicago building code and have never once heard of a switchback. The pie arrived at a tailgate, asked for a fork, and was told this is Arkansas, everybody has a fork.

news.title: Lake-effect cheese advisory issued for Northwest Arkansas
news.text: Forecasters tracking a cold front off Lake Michigan say it picked up a dangerous amount of mozzarella over Illinois and is now settling along I-49. Residents from Bentonville to Springdale should expect accumulations of two to three inches, mostly on deep-dish crusts. Shovels are not recommended. Forks are.

news.title: Chicago transplant learns “Woo Pig Sooie” is not a topping
news.text: A recent arrival from Wicker Park reportedly tried to order a large Woo Pig Sooie with extra Sooie, under the impression it was a regional sausage. faq.question: Is Windy Holler a real restaurant?
faq.answer: No. Windy Holler is a parody pizzeria. Every name, address, phone number, dish, price, and story here is invented, and it is not affiliated with any real restaurant or with the University of Arkansas.

faq.question: When are you open?
faq.answer: On paper: 11 am–10 pm Monday through Thursday, 11 am–midnight Friday and Saturday, and noon–9 pm Sunday. In practice, never. We are fictional.

faq.question: What is tavern cut?
faq.answer: Thin crust cut into squares instead of wedges, the way Chicago bars have long served it. The corner pieces are the prize.

faq.question: Is Chicago-style deep dish a casserole?
faq.answer: It is a pizza that has made some bold life choices. Every pizza here comes deep dish or tavern-cut thin, so you can pick your side of the argument.

faq.question: Do I really need a fork for the deep dish?
faq.answer: You don't need one. You'll want one. A knife helps too.

faq.question: Can I book a room for a party?
faq.answer: Fayetteville has the Bleacher Room and Rogers has the Upper Deck. Both are fictional, so they are always available and never bookable.

faq.question: When is trivia night?
faq.answer: Wednesdays at 7 pm at every location, with half-price sorghum wings. Texarkana asks every question twice, once in each state.

faq.question: Why is there okra in the giardiniera?
faq.answer: Giardiniera is just pickled vegetables that moved to Chicago, and pickled okra is the most Arkansas pickle there is. It stays crisp, carries heat, and has never once been slimy in our care.

faq.question: What is chocolate gravy?
faq.answer: An Ozark breakfast: cocoa, sugar, butter, and milk cooked into a pourable gravy and spooned over hot biscuits. We pour it over a skillet brownie, which is the same idea after 5 pm.

faq.question: Can I get ketchup?
faq.answer: On fries, yes. On anything shaped like a hot dog, we'll need to see two forms of ID.
